items.title: Neuromorphic BrailleNet: accurate and generalizable braille reading beyond single characters through event-based optical tactile sensing
items.summary: Abstract Replicating fluid, human-like Braille reading requires artificial tactile systems that can maintain high recognition accuracy across varying contact depths and scanning speeds. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Leakage‐Controlled Evaluation of Pixel‐Level MRI–sCT Fusion Reveals a Quality–Performance Mismatch in Brain Tumour Classification
items.summary: ABSTRACT In medical image classification, pixel‐level fusion has been presupposed to be useful in merging complementary visual information and improving classification performance. In this research, we test this assumption by considering fused‐image quality and image‐level leakage‐controlled classification performance for MRI–sCT brain tumour analysis. Seven EfficientNet‐B0 input representations were evaluated on 1,469 test image pairs from four classes (glioma, meningioma, no‐tumour and pituitary). Because patient identifiers were unavailable, patient‐level independence could not be verified.
